serotype_evidence.value: Salmonella enterica subsp. enterica serovar Typhimurium

curation.notes: High-quality reference isolate from FDA surveillance. Both reads and assembly available.

reads.download_cmd: fasterq-dump --gzip --outdir data/ SRR1234567 && mv data/SRR1234567_1.fastq.gz data/reads_1.fq.gz && mv data/SRR1234567_2.fastq.gz data/reads_2.fq.gz

assembly.download_cmd: datasets download genome accession GCA_001234567.1 --include genome --filename data/assembly.zip && unzip -j data/assembly.zip '*/genomic.fna' -d data/ && mv data/genomic.fna data/contigs.fa && rm data/assembly.zip

SeqSero2.run_cmd: SeqSero2_package.py -m a -t 4 -i data/reads_1.fq.gz data/reads_2.fq.gz -d actual/seqsero2/ -n seqsero2

SeqSero2S.run_cmd: SeqSero2S_package.py -m a -t 4 -i data/reads_1.fq.gz data/reads_2.fq.gz -d actual/seqsero2s/ -n seqsero2s

validation_instructions.serological: Typhimurium is the most common Salmonella serotype in US clinical isolates. Accept exact match 'Typhimurium' (case-insensitive) or full subspecies designation 'Salmonella enterica subsp. enterica serovar Typhimurium'. Antigenic formula must match 1,4,[5],12:i:1,2 with O antigens (1,4,[5],12) and H antigens (i:1,2). Note that bracket notation around '5' may be omitted by some tools - accept '1,4,5,12:i:1,2' as correct. Monophasic variant '1,4,[5],12:i:-' is PARTIAL (correct O and H1 but missing H2 phase). ST19 is the dominant sequence type for Typhimurium globally.
validation_instructions.mlst: Expected ST19, which is the most common sequence type for Salmonella Typhimurium. Also accept ST34 as PARTIAL - it is a single-locus variant (aroC allele difference) commonly found in clinical isolates and considered closely related. Any other ST is a FAIL unless novel alleles are reported, which should be flagged for manual review.

notes: Representative high-frequency serotype used as positive control. Tests basic serotyping accuracy and common MLST profile.
